title: When a Dragon Moves In
author: Jodi Moore
intro: A young boy builds a perfect sandcastle at the beach. Right away, a dragon moves in!
checkedAgainst: Storyline Online page and teacher guide

questions.q: Where is the boy spending the day with his family?
questions.clue: There is sand, waves, and the ocean.
questions.yes: The boy and his family are at the beach.

questions.q: What does the boy build in the sand?
questions.clue: He uses his bucket and shovel to build a home for a dragon.

questions.q: Who moves into the boy's sandcastle?
questions.clue: It is a creature with wings, scales, and smoke.
questions.yes: A red dragon moves into the sandcastle.

questions.q: How does the boy feel when he finds the dragon?
questions.clue: He thinks he is very lucky to have a new friend.
questions.yes: The boy is delighted to have a dragon friend.

questions.q: Why will a beach bully stay away from the sandcastle?
questions.clue: The creature living inside the castle scares bullies away.
questions.yes: A beach bully would never stomp a castle with a dragon inside.

questions.q: What fun things do the boy and the dragon do together?

options.text: Fly a kite and roast marshmallows

questions.clue: They play in the wind and toast sweet treats.
questions.yes: They roam the beach, fly a kite, and roast marshmallows.

questions.q: Why does the boy hide the dragon's smoke?

options.text: So the lifeguard does not see it
So the seagulls do not cough
So the sun stays bright and warm

questions.clue: Someone whose job is to keep the beach safe might see it.
questions.yes: He hides the dragon's smoke from the lifeguard.

questions.q: What does Mum think the dragon's roar is?
questions.clue: She is reading her book and hears the crashing waves.
questions.yes: Mum thinks the sound is the roar of the ocean.

questions.q: What does Dad say the dragon's feather really is?
questions.clue: It comes from a white bird you see at the beach.
questions.yes: Dad thinks the feather is from a seagull.

questions.q: What does the boy's family say the dragon's teeth are?
questions.clue: Waves wash these hard sea pieces onto the sand.
questions.yes: His family says the dragon's teeth are broken shells.

questions.q: What happens to the family's food at the picnic?

options.text: Sandwiches vanish and brownies have claw prints
Apples roll into the salty ocean water
Ice cream melts all over the towels

questions.clue: The dragon eats the lunch and steps in the chocolate treats.
questions.yes: The sandwiches disappear and claw prints are in the brownies.

questions.q: What happens to the boy's big sister that gets him in trouble?

options.text: Sand is sprayed all over her
Cold water is splashed on her
Seaweed is dropped on her head

questions.clue: The boy blames the dragon for throwing beach grit at her.
questions.yes: Sand is thrown all over his big sister.

questions.q: How do the boy's parents feel after all the mischief?
questions.clue: They have had enough of this dragon business.
questions.yes: His parents are frustrated because of all the trouble.

questions.q: What does the boy tell the dragon to do?

options.text: Leave until he learns some manners
Go to sleep in the castle
Fly home to his mum and dad

questions.clue: The dragon was being too naughty and rude.
questions.yes: He orders the dragon to leave until he learns some manners.

questions.q: When does the boy build an even better sandcastle?
questions.clue: He only waits until the very next day.
questions.yes: He builds an even bigger sandcastle the next day.
